The inverse of the matrix $N$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to the blank spaces?

$$
\begin{aligned}[N\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

question.worked_solution:
We write down $N$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $N$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[N\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}↔\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${N}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{N}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
